body:
Gold prices across both platforms are pricing spot bullion in the low-$4,300s to $4,400s, which lines up with actual news flow: gold futures opened at $4,400 on August 10, 2026 and were trading near $4,391 shortly after.

Gold (GC=F) December futures opened at $4,400 per troy ounce on Monday, August 10, 2026, flat compared to Friday's closing price, with the price edging down to $4,391.50 shortly after the open. That backdrop explains why Kalshi's above $4,371.99 by August 31 contract sits almost exactly at a coin-flip (52¢ bid, 57¢ ask) and why the year-end $4,300 and $4,400 strikes are both trading well above 50 — the market is pricing gold as already near those levels with room to drift either way into year-end.

The scanner surfaced exactly one cross-platform opportunity today, and it's not worth acting on. It pairs a 4¢ YES on Polymarket's hit $4,700 in August (a touch contract, meaning it pays out if gold ever trades above $4,700 intramonth) with a 95¢ NO on Kalshi's above $4,771.99 at 5pm ET, August 31 (a settle contract, paying out only on the closing print). Buying both costs 99¢ for a payout that's proven to always be worth $1, but after fees the edge is under a penny per contract and the scanner could only size it to 100 contracts — about 67 cents of total profit. That Kalshi strike also shows zero 24-hour volume, so the 95¢ ask is a stale, thin quote rather than a tradable price; the mismatch is really just two different contract designs (touch vs. settle, $4,700 vs. $4,771.99) brushing up against each other at the edges of illiquid books, not a real arbitrage.

Beyond that, it was a quiet session — no other mispricings between Kalshi's settle-style ladder and Polymarket's touch/direction contracts, and no unusual spread or single-contract move that stood out from the broader $4,300–$4,500 range gold has been consolidating in.
headline: Gold consolidates near $4,400; one cross-platform 'edge' is a stale-quote mirage

sources.title: Gold prices today, Monday, August 10, 2026: Highest opening price since early June
